evidence.observation: Nodes expose explicit element IDs, parent/child links, local/geometric transforms, matrices, native Euler order and inherit modes. element_id is stable when loading the same file, not after re-export. Scene settings expose original axes, unit_meters and frames_per_second. Scope identities to the immutable file revision; names are labels.

Conversion modes may modify root transforms, add scale/geometry helpers, compensate inherits or modify geometry. PRESERVE modes expose the originals and require proper special-inheritance evaluation. FighterPort must retain original native hierarchy and binds, and treat converted/evaluated representations as explicitly derived views; do not invoke helper-generation or geometry modification as invisible canonicalization.

Per-vertex weight_begin/num_weights address a variable-length weight array; max_weights_per_vertex is reported. There is no four/eight-influence representation ceiling in these arrays. Raw weights need not sum to one. Clusters expose geometry_to_bone, mesh_node_to_bone, bind_to_world and current geometry_to_world. Skinning methods include rigid, linear, dual-quaternion and blended DQ/linear.

The evaluator loops every listed influence, handles DQ/linear blending, and normalizes the accumulated result by total_weight. Preserve raw source weights separately; evaluating its specified normalized skin policy does not authorize rewriting weights or silently truncating to FighterPort's current four slots.

Raw animated properties/layers and double-second key times expose constant-previous, constant-next, linear and cubic Bezier segments with split time/value tangents plus extrapolation modes. Bake options include step handling and key reduction; rotation reduction assumes spherical interpolation. Preserve original Euler winding/layers/curves separately; a quaternion bake is not a lossless native curve copy.

Concrete curve and transform evaluators and an animation bake entry point exist; use them offline behind a provider. They are not a retarget/contact solver and must not become decode/evaluation preparation in playback ticks.
SPHERIC rotation order remains accompanied by a TODO about its meaning. Do not claim every native rotation mode; detect and independently test unusual modes instead of relabeling them supported.

evidence.observation: Native indexed nodes retain hierarchy and matrix or TRS local representations. System.Numerics evaluation uses local*parent; precise world accumulation uses double matrices internally. Matrix-setting on animated TRS nodes is restricted. ApplyBasisTransform can add a parent node, so it is not an acceptable hidden rewrite of an imported native graph.

Skin joints reference indexed Node objects and correspond to IBM accessor entries; missing IBMs are identity via GetJoint. BindJoints convenience overloads recompute inverse bindings from current worlds, and the supplied-IBM overload validates/sanitizes affine matrix entries. Read original accessors and preserve bytes; do not invoke rebind/sanitization as preservation of exact imported native bind data.

STEP/LINEAR and CUBICSPLINE APIs retain input key times, quaternion/vector values and separate incoming/outgoing cubic tangents. Morphs have both a bounded SparseWeight8 API and an unlimited float[]/ArraySegment API. Use original typed arrays/curves for provenance; glTF quaternion animation is not an authored Euler-turn history.

The pinned implementation also represents animation pointer targets beyond ordinary node TRS. Merely retaining a pointer is not proof that FighterPort can evaluate/edit the target material/camera/property or encode it into another game.

Explicitly capped at eight nonzero weights; constructors retain the eight heaviest/most representative values when input is larger. This convenience representation cannot be used as the lossless source skin/morph store.
Toolkit vertex skinning representations are explicitly four/eight influence variants. Do not silently reduce full source weights through these builders.
Raw attribute dictionaries/accessors permit retaining original JOINTS_n/WEIGHTS_n data independent of convenience vertex structs. Full-influence interpretation still needs a verified adapter path.
The inspected skin validation explicitly checks JOINTS_0/1 and WEIGHTS_0/1 only. Do not infer complete >8 influence validation from the general attribute dictionary or from successful load.

evidence.observation: The low-level v1.0 skeleton retains ordered bone entries, u16 index/i16 parent, flags and all four native local/world/inverse matrix arrays. Native names are strings; low-level numeric IDs/order must remain asset scoped.

The high-level representation retains only local transform/parent/name/billboard data and regenerates world and inverse arrays during output. It is not a lossless substitute for the low-level/original native skeleton. Explicit noncommuting-parent tests are required for matrix conventions; no runtime math acceptance was run here.

High-level weights are variable-length per-bone Vec<VertexWeight>, not four influences. Writer counts per-vertex influences then casts max count to u8; v1.10 writes u16 vertex indices with an explicit overflow error and f32 weights. No automatic four/eight-weight truncation is established here; adapter must validate true format budgets and duplicates.

A source TODO states rigging unk1 is not preserved for some single-bound meshes; writer sets unk1=1 and sorts rigging groups. This high-level path cannot support a blanket unrelated-resource/byte-preservation claim.

Animation versions 1.2/2.0/2.1 expose final_frame_index, groups/nodes/tracks, quaternion TRS, UV transforms, Float, PatternIndex, Boolean and Vector4 channels. Frame arrays store one value per frame; one value repeats through final_frame_index. Scale compensation and override flags are separate native semantics. No native rational FPS/unit convention is established by these data structures; obtain game/provider context rather than assuming Brawl semantics.

The ordinary writer implements supported versions with codec selection. to_anim_uncompressed implements v1.2 but v2.0 and v2.1 are literal todo!() branches. Do not call that API for those versions or claim an implemented guaranteed-uncompressed path. Non-Boolean compressed tracks are documented lossy.

Real v2 codec entry points select compression based on data type/frame count and preserve separate frame count/transform flags. final_frame_index must be nonnegative and at least max track count minus one. Decode success is not exact transform/channel preservation after lossy encoding.
Read the pinned compression implementation as the native codec boundary, not a universal curve/retarget algorithm. Existing Brawl integer-float and I12 corrections remain separate and unchanged.

decision.excludedUse: No claim of exact uncompressed 2.x output, full native byte preservation through ssbh_data reconstruction, active game-material behavior, actor/articles/gameplay, model porting or in-game acceptance. Do not relabel all sampled tracks as generic CHR0 curves.
